item.title: Omicho Market: Kanazawa's Kitchen for Nearly 300 Years — Guide
item.description: Omicho Market, nicknamed ‘Kanazawa’s Kitchen’, has supplied the city with fresh seafood, produce and local specialties for nearly 300 years, its narrow covered lanes lined with roughly 180 stalls selling everything from Kaga vegetables to premium crab and the region’s prized nodoguro fish. Beyond the stalls themselves, several small eateries within and around the market serve the day’s catch directly, making it a popular spot for a fresh seafood breakfast or lunch alongside its role as a working local market.

item.title: Toyama Bay Sushi: Where the Bay's Rich Waters Meet the Sushi Counter — Guide
item.description: Toyama Bay is known among Japanese sushi enthusiasts as a premier source of fresh seafood, fed by nutrient-rich currents and an unusually steep underwater topography that brings deep-water and shallow-water species into close proximity, yielding a wide variety of fish and shellfish landed daily at local ports. Sushi in Toyama ranges from affordable conveyor-belt kaiten-zushi restaurants, several of which are considered among the best of their kind in Japan, to high-end sushi counters showcasing the bay’s specialty catches, including shiro-ebi and hotaru-ika alongside more familiar seasonal fish.

item.title: Wajima Morning Market: One of Japan's Oldest Asaichi — Guide
item.description: Wajima Morning Market, or asaichi, has operated daily for over a thousand years, making it one of Japan’s oldest continuously running street markets, lining a stretch of central Wajima with dozens of small family-run stalls each morning. Vendors, many of them older women who have run the same stall for decades, sell fresh seafood caught along the Noto Peninsula coast, local produce and pickles, alongside Wajima’s famous lacquerware, offering visitors a genuine glimpse of daily life in this coastal fishing town.
